result.rationale: The diff changes deleteEvent's fallback from `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, but this branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the find predicate can never match and calendarId is always undefined. This is a real regression introduced by the diff: previously the fallback returned the destination calendar's externalId, now it always returns undefined for bookings whose reference lacks externalCalendarId, breaking deletion of the Google calendar event.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now compute the fallback calendar ID as `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. If `externalCalendarId` is `undefined/null`, that predicate can never match a real `externalId`, so the fallback resolves to `undefined` even when `event.destinationCalendar` contains valid calendars. This is exactly the “dead predicate” described in the finding, and it can cause deletes/updates to target no calendar (or rely on later defaults that may not exist), breaking cancellation cleanup for bookings whose reference lacks `externalCalendarId`.
